claim: Experimental values are not independent repeats: 419 unique parent molecules carry 543 observations, 86 molecules contribute >1 row, within-molecule spread mean 13.42 / median 11.90 / max 47.9 kcal/mol, and the correct pooled within-molecule SD is ~9.97, not the ~165 produced by a naive pooled-variance computation.
value_found: 419 unique parent molecules; 543 observations; 86 multi-row molecules carrying 210 rows (333 singletons); within-molecule spread (max-min, multi-row molecules only) mean 13.418605 (13.42), median 11.900000 (11.90), max 47.900000 (47.9); pooled within-molecule SD = sqrt(sum_g (n_g-1)s_g^2 / sum_g(n_g-1)) = 9.965372 (dof=124); unweighted mean-of-variances variant = 10.315528; n-weighted (ddof=0-style) variant = 10.110236; the ~165 figure = 165.2622713321, exactly reproduced as sqrt( sum_g (n_g-1)s_g^4 / sum_g(n_g-1) ). Every reported digit matches.
unit: Raw benchmark row = one experimental bond observation (543 rows, 543 unique observation_ids, 0 exact duplicate rows). Within-molecule grouping key = parent_structure_smiles; grouping is identical under RDKit canonicalisation (419 unique canonical SMILES, 86 multi-row). Spread computed only on the 86 molecules with n_g>1. Pooled SD is the df-weighted within-group pooling over those 86 groups; independently confirmed by a one-way ANOVA residual SD over all 543 rows with molecule as factor (identical: sqrt(SS_res/124)=9.965372).
method: Own script /tmp/verify11/verify_11.py (+ forensic165.py, units.py, final.py), written without importing the workstream modules. Read only data/normalized_views/experimental_benchmark.tsv (sha256 319bf2c88ab47bb2c7f779163ed48cd2f316e6299eeda0b999d924ffe81ad484) with pandas; used groupby(parent_structure_smiles) on experimental_bde_kcal_mol. Pooled SD computed 4 independent ways: (A) sum-of-squares pooling, (B) one-way ANOVA residual SD via explicit demeaning over all 543 rows, (C) unweighted mean of group variances, (D) RMS within-group deviation with n-k denominator - A, B and D agree to 1e-6 (9.965372). Range spread recomputed independently with np.ptp. The naive-formula search was exhaustive over 14 numerator quantities x 9 divisors.
notes: All headline numbers reproduce exactly from the raw TSV. IMPORTANT NUANCE ON THE '160s' STORY, NOT ON THE HEADLINE: no ordinary naive pooled-variance formula actually produces 165. Exhaustive search: unweighted mean-of-variances gives 10.3155; n-weighted pooling gives 10.1102; sqrt of the SUM of group variances gives 95.66; the pooled VARIANCE (unsqrted) is 99.31; total SD ignoring grouping is 13.39; between-molecule SD of means is 11.28. The ONLY formula that lands on 165.2622713321 (match to 1e-10) is sqrt( sum_g (n_g-1)s_g^4 / sum_g (n_g-1) ), i.e. the per-group variance squared a SECOND time inside the weighted average. This is a code defect, not a naive estimator: it is present verbatim at output/analysis/ws5_het.py line 24, 'np.sqrt(np.average((var.to_numpy(float))**2, weights=g['size'].to_numpy()-1))'. The quantity has units of kcal^2 (it is the RMS of the per-molecule variances), so it cannot be an SD at all. A prior verifier note in output/results/verify_3_channel_accuracy.json already documented this same root cause, and I independently reproduced it. STABILITY: the 9.97 value is robust - leave-one-molecule-out ranges only 9.530 (drop C#CCC, the 47.9 spread outlier) to 10.094 (drop CCCCCC) across all 86 deletions; dropping the worst molecule shifts it to 9.53, still nowhere near 165. ANALYSIS-UNIT CHECK: grouping by fragment pair instead of parent molecule gives only 4 multi-row groups with pooled SD 1.537, so the 9.97 is specific to and correctly labelled as the parent-molecule unit; no parent molecule has two rows with the same (molecule, fragment pair) key, so molecule is the operative repeat unit. CAVEAT ON INTERPRETATION (inherited from the claim, not a recomputation error): 9.97 kcal/mol is the pooling of differences BETWEEN different bonds in the same molecule, so it mixes genuine bond-type variation with literature disagreement; it is an upper bound on reference-value scatter, not a pure measurement-repeatability estimate. Consistent with this, 1 of the 86 multi-row molecules has all-identical values and eta^2 (between-molecule share of experimental variance) is 0.873, so most experimental variance is between-molecule rather than within-molecule.
